text:
hema: quick thread - Finance raised edge cases where cost ended up attributed to the default tenant because enrichment happened after we exported billing rows. thinking a design that: 1) declares `billing.phase` as required at ingress, 2) holds traces short window for reconciliation, and 3) apportion work across forked children using a `billing.work_units` field. thoughts?

owen: +1 to an explicit schema. the current implicit tagging causes non-determinism. small ask: make the reconcile window pluggable per-tenant (high-volume tenants might want shorter windows).

lucy: agree on `billing.work_units`. default should be 1.0 and we Validate: non-negative float. apportionment algorithm: child_cost = parent_cost * (child.work_units / sum(child.work_units)). simple and deterministic.

marc: implementation nuances: reconciliation must run before any sampling decision that would drop spans used for later attribution. otherwise we lose the chance to rewrite. pipeline order suggestion: ingress-validation -> reconcile-window -> sampling/retention -> storage/export.

hema: rough config proposal:```yaml
billing_reconcile:
  enabled: true
  default_window_seconds: 5
  per_tenant_overrides: true
  max_parent_hops: 3
  strict_mode: false  # if true, reject ambiguous attribution at ingest
```

owen: metrics to add: `billing.uncertain_count`, `billing.rewrites_total`, `billing.rewrite_latency_p50/p95`, `billing.rewrite_memory_bytes`. alerts: rewrite_rate > baseline * 5 should page on-call.

lucy: edge-case: what if enrichment forks to many children and only some have `work_units` set? we should assume default 1.0 for missing values and log a warning on the span owner. also require `billing.parent_span_id` when forking so reconciler can stitch.

marc: reconcile cost: we buffer traces for window -> memory ~= avg_pending_traces * avg_span_size. we should model with a histogram. for canary use defaults: avg_span 800 bytes, expected pending 10k => ~8MB/sec. include in RFC.

hema: finance needs auditability: when we rewrite, emit an audit event with fields: `original_export_line_id`, `rewrite_reason`, `apportioned_amounts` and include `signed_by` service id. store audit events in a low-ttl audit table (90 days).

owen: for deterministic billing exports, reconciler must emit a `billing.rewrite=1` tag on adjusted spans and include `billing.export_version` so downstream consumers know a rewrite occurred and which algorithm version was used.

lucy: sampling policy: for reconcile window to work, we must disable early sampling for traces in the pending set. sampling decision should be delayed until reconciliation completes (or window expires). heavy implication for memory and latency. add canary parameter `max_pending_traces_per_shard` to bound memory.

marc: propose a graceful fallback: if pending set exceeds threshold, mark trace `billing.attribution=best_effort` and continue; also emit `reconcile_overflow` metric. avoids head-of-line blocking.

hema: acceptance criteria for canary: 1) p95 export latency increase < 200ms, 2) `billing_uncertain_count` reduced by >= 90% for synthetic delayed-enrich workload, 3) memory overhead within modeled expectation. abort if p95 export latency regresses > 500ms or reconciliation_overflow_rate > 1% sustained 5m.

owen: canary plan: staging run synthetic delayed-enrichment tails (Weibull shape=0.7) across 1k traces/sec; measure metrics. roll to us-central canary for 24h with 5% traffic.

lucy: test vectors: single-child late-key, multi-child fork with uniform work_units, missing work_units, >max_parent_hops, preempted parent key. include unit tests for apportioner and integration tests for pipeline ordering.

marc: ops tasks: update ingestion validator, implement reconcile service, add billing exporter change, add audit sink, add dashboards/alerts. I'll create the checklist.

billing-bot: ticket created: INGEST-APPORTION-778. canary scheduled: us-central-1 -> 2026-04-05 03:00 UTC.

hema: OK I'll draft the follow-up RFC with config, metrics, acceptance, perf model, and sample export rows. assigning owners: marc (infra), lucy (apportioner), owen (metrics & canary). i'll post link here when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
